newsitem.title: GREECE: Greece's Silver & Baryte dismisses merger woes.
newsitem.headline: Greece's Silver & Baryte dismisses merger woes.

text.p: Shares of ore processor Silver & Baryte traded substantially lower on Wednesday on news of squeezed 1996 pre-tax profit by a 1.1 billion drachma extraordinary provision due to its merger with affiliated Bauxites Parnasse.
Silver & Baryte launched an extensive workforce reduction programme for Bauxites Parnasse, Greece's major miner and exporter of bauxite ore, which it absorbed in mid-1996.
Redundancies in Bauxite Parnasse have given rise to large extraordinary payments.
Silver & Baryte management received heavy criticism in 1996 when plans for its merger with affiliated Bauxites Parnasse were unveiled.
But on Wednesday management dismissed views by market participants which echoed this criticism.

"I believe the merger has been beneficial to Silver & Baryte because it has helped the cost rationalisation programme currently being implemented," finance director Stratis Papaefstratiou told Reuters.
There was enough room for corporate moves aiming at building a very strong corporation, he said.
Asked whether investors were aware of the possibility of extraordinary provisions following the merger, he said the decision to post the provision item was taken only recently.

"No mention of the likelihood of extraordinary provisions was made last year when plans for the merger were presented to the investment community. The workforce reduction plan came into being in 1997. At that time there were only initial thoughts of such changes," Papaefstratiou said.
"The merger led us to pursue a wider-ranging cost rationalisation plan than initially planned," he added.
"We had forecast 3.7-3.8 billion drachmas for fiscal 1996 pre-tax earnings which was realised on a pre-provision basis," he said.
The probability of further provisions being posted in the future was very thin.

"No additional provisions are required, though we will need to monitor closely the margin by which the total cost of labour cuts shall fall short of the 1.1 billion provision item," Papaefstratiou said.
Silver & Baryte's shares lost 300 drachmas, closing 6.59 percent lower at 4,250 after hitting a low of 4,186, down 8.0 percent, in early trade. The stock was active on volume of 121,420 shares.
Silver & Baryte had posted pre-tax earnings of 3.06 billion drachmas in fiscal 1995, distributing a per share dividend of 140 drachmas.
It intends to pay the same dividend to its shareholders for 1996, despite the fall in profit. --Angelos Kiosklis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
